notes:
Lead profile: small-but-growing support automation vendor. Self-serve preferred, wants hosted API for speed-to-market.

Key technical notes / customer quotes: 
- "We have predictable baseline traffic (~15-25 RPS) but marketing/feature releases cause short spikes to ~150-200 RPS for up to 2 minutes."
- "429s currently trigger for us during spikes — we'd prefer automatic short-lived burst capacity or clear guidance for client-side backoff patterns."
- Client latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for short chat completions (acceptable up to 500ms for complex rerank calls).
- Throughput sensitivity: cost-conscious; wants batching/embedding caching suggestions to reduce token spend.
- Model preference: open models (quantized) initially; open to Redwood model suggestions based on cost/latency tradeoffs.

Rate-limit / quota needs described in call: 
- Need temporary burst window for POC: allow concurrency to jump to 250 concurrent tokens/requests for 5 minutes during scheduled campaigns.
- Want soft quota warnings via webhook or header before 429s, and an SLA for quota bump for paying accounts.
- Ask for recommended client-side retry/backoff (e.g., jittered exponential with max retries 5, and 429-handling with Retry-After header usage).

Security/compliance: SOC2 required; retention_controls and audit logs asked for but currently comfortable with Redwood hosted if SOC2 + audit logs available. No VPC/on-prem requirement now.

Business: Trial goal is to validate no-regret switch to hosted API for initial product. If POC handles bursts with acceptable 429 behavior and cost projections look good, options to upgrade to reserved Dedicated in 6-9 months.

Questions outstanding / action items: 
- AE: Provide sample rate-limit config templates and recommended client retry logic.
- SE: Configure sandbox keys with extended burst quota for scheduled POC window (2026-03-10 to 2026-03-12).
- Pricing: Provide one-off burst pricing or demo throttling tiers for SMB.
- Security: Share SOC2 attestation and audit log retention policy (link to drive doc).
use_case_summary: Primary: agent-assist chat for support reps with embeddings-powered KB retrieval and a light reranking step. Workload has low baseline RPS but frequent short spikes tied to email campaigns and product launches. Needs hosted-api for self-serve onboarding; cost-sensitive and wants guidance to avoid token waste via batching and caching.
technical_requirements:
- Baseline concurrency: 15-25 RPS
- Burst behavior: short spikes to 150-200 RPS (customer asks for safe headroom to 250)
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms (500ms acceptable for heavy paths)
- Retry behavior: respect Retry-After, recommend jittered exponential backoff, max 5 retries
- Metrics: per-key 429 count, per-route latency, token spend per user session
- Prefer public cloud-hosted APIs, no VPC required for POC
po_notes: Customer is early-stage SMB but could convert to salary-backed ARR if POC succeeds. Emphasize self-serve onboarding, clear documentation on quotas, and a simple path to request temporary increases. Keep pricing transparent; small teams dislike hidden burst fees.
sales_playbook_recs:
- Offer time-limited burst allowance for trial with clear telemetry window.
- Provide a short "Handling 429s" runbook for engineers (code snippets + best practices).
- Schedule 30-min post-POC review to walk telemetry and cost numbers.
- Suggest Redwood Optimize tips: prefix caching for common prompts and embedding reuse.
